draft.title: The National Employment Standards
card: The National Employment Standards (NES) are 11 minimum conditions set by law. Every employee in the national workplace relations system gets them.
They include a maximum of 38 ordinary hours a week, plus reasonable additional hours. They also cover leave, such as annual leave, personal/carer's leave and parental leave.
They also include notice of termination. This is the warning an employer must give, or pay for, when ending a job, and it is longer for staff who have worked there longer.
The NES are a floor, not a ceiling. A contract or award can give an employee more, but it cannot give less.
draft.remember: The NES are the minimum. An employer can offer more but never less.

a.q: Which statement about the National Employment Standards is correct?
opts: An employer may offer more than them but not less
An employer may offer less if the employee agrees
They only apply to full-time staff in large firms
They are suggestions that an employer can choose to follow
a.why: The NES are a legal minimum, so a contract can add to them but cannot go below them. Agreeing to less does not remove them, because they are a floor that the law sets.
a.clue: Think of the NES as a floor.

b.q: Ravi owns a bakery in Ballarat. He hires Dana and says she will get no annual leave, because she accepted that in her contract. Which is the best response?
opts: The contract is not allowed to remove her NES leave
The contract is fine because Dana agreed to it
The contract is fine because the bakery is a small business
The contract is fine if Ravi pays a higher hourly wage
b.why: Annual leave is part of the NES, so a contract cannot take it away, even if the employee agrees. Small size or a higher wage does not remove the minimum, so these options are wrong.
b.clue: Can agreement take away a legal minimum?

a.best: An employer may offer more than them but not less

b.best: The contract is not allowed to remove her NES leave

check.summary: No problems found. The NES facts are correct (11 standards, a 38-hour maximum, leave and notice), both questions have one clear right answer, and the explanations match the card.
